eval_split: V_where (local render_mode only), normal-only (winner_confidence != low excluded)
metric: matched-area top-k IoU: k = gt_area_k(gt_low), pred_k = topk_mask(field, k), gt_k = topk_mask(gt_low, k), hard_iou(pred_k, gt_k)  [q3vl/whereb/metrics.py]
selection_rule: per family: the 15 samples with the largest max-min top-k IoU across all 7 arms (published eval_final/per_sample.jsonl, mode=generated, normal-only), then the 3 of those with the largest max-min across the five non-degenerate arms (ST_LANG/SEGSAM/MATTE/SAMDEC/LIIF), de-duplicated on the (ST_LANG,MATTE,SAMDEC,LIIF) IoU tuple

ST_LANG.note_std_float32: field_std is the float32 std of the raw field; a single-valued field can still report ~3e-08 from float32 rounding, so n_unique==1 is the exact test

SEGSAM.note_std_float32: field_std is the float32 std of the raw field; a single-valued field can still report ~3e-08 from float32 rounding, so n_unique==1 is the exact test

notes: torch.topk tie-breaking is not identical on CPU and CUDA.  Every number here was computed on the same device the published board used (CUDA); the per-arm `topk_iou_cpu_recompute` column is the CPU value of the same field, kept so the difference is visible rather than silent.

measured 12/12: CONDINST's top-k mask equals 'the first k cells in flattened raster order' -- the field is exactly 1.0 in every cell, so the mask is a tie-break artefact of topk and carries no prediction.
reconstruction_check_max_abs_delta is 0.0 for all seven arms: the captured top-k IoU reproduces eval_final/per_sample.jsonl (mode=generated) bit for bit.
